div.head: Norðleoda 1
div.ab: Norðleoda cynges gild is XXX þusend þrymsa: fiftene þusend þrymsa bið þæs wergildes, XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebirað magum ⁊ seo cynebot þam leodum.
Cynges wergild is inne mid Englum on folcriht XXX þusend þrymsa: XV þusend ðrymsa byð þæs weres ⁊ XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebyreð þam magum ⁊ seo cynebot þam leodum.

Ðæs cyninges wergyld sie mid Engla cynne on folcriht ðryttig ðusend ðrimsa: ⁊ ðæra XV m. sien ðæs wæres ⁊ oþra XV m. ðæs cynedomes; se wære belympaþ to ðam mægþe ðæs cynecynnes ⁊ þ' cynebot to ðam landleod.

Regis weregildum est cum Anglis in (iure) publico recto XXX milia þrimsa: id est XV milia þrimsa sunt de wera et XV milia cynedomes, id est regie dignitatis (censure); ipsum natalis eius pretium pertinet cognationi et cynebot ipsius terrę nationi.
Cynges wergild is inne mid Englum on folcriht XXX þusend þrymsa: XV þusend ðrymsa byð þæs weres and XV þusend þæs cynedomes; se wer gebyreð þam magum and seo cynebot þam leodum.

Entgelt (Wergeld hlq) für den König der Nordleute ist volksrechtlich [im Lande H] (bei den Engländern hlq) 30 000 Tremissen [375 Pfund]: (und von denen seien Ld) 15 000 Tremissen ist [Betrag] des Wergeldes (und) 15 000 [der] der Königswürde; das Wergeld gebührt den Verwandten (gehört der Sippe des Königsgeschlechts Ld) und die Königsbusse dem Volke (des Landes lq).

The payment (wergild, hlq) for the king of the North-people is by folk-right [in the land, H] (among the English, hlq) 30,000 thrymsas [375 pounds]: (and of these let there be, Ld) 15,000 thrymsas [as the sum] of the wergild (and) 15,000 [that] of the kingship; the wergild belongs to the kinsmen (belongs to the kin of the royal house, Ld) and the king-compensation to the people (of the land, lq).

The payment for a king of the North people is 30,000 thrymsas; 15,000 thrymsas belong to the wergild, 15,000 to the kingship; the wergild belongs to the kinsmen and the royal-compensation to the people.

According to the folk law of the English people, a king’s wergild is thirty thousand thrymsas: fifteen thousand thrymsas are for the man and fifteen thousand thrymsas are for the kingship. The personal wergild belongs to his kinsmen and the royal compensation belongs to the people.
div.note: H's ‘inne mid Englum’ is a corruption in hlq (compare Grið 4). D supplies ‘on folcriht’ from the others and Mirce 3. Liebermann compares Mirce 3.1 and 4.; AY: corrected against Rabin p. 12, October 2026 (was “∅; ∅; ∅”, now “|; |; |”); AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 12, October 2026 (was “[title]; ∅”, now “∅; |”); AX: pages in Rabin (text / translation), checked against Rabin (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “12”, now “12 / 13”; 1 rows of Norðleoda)

On Wergild: The earlier version of the Compilation titles this text The Law of the Northern People. A major component of Wulfstan’s revision was to diminish the regional specificity of the individual texts, though this should not be taken as a sign that the wergild values listed here necessarily applied south of the Humber.
a king’s wergild: Cambridge, Corpus Christi College MS 201 reads, “The wergild of a king of the northern people.”

thrymsas: The term “thrymsa” was used both as a general term for coins and more specifically as the equivalent of one-third of a shilling, about four pennies. It is the latter meaning which most likely applies here.

Wenn die Zufügung, die on folces folcriht (Mirce 3) gleichsteht, einen Sondersinn, hinausgehend über ‘gemeinrechtlich, landesüblich’ birgt, so bed. sie: ‘nach alter theoretischer Überlieferung, die nur gilt, wenn es überhaupt zur Gerichtsverhandlung kommt, was in der Regel nicht der Fall ist, da den erschlagenen König entweder sein Geschlecht oder Gefolge blutig rächt, oder statutarisches Königsrecht dem Mörder Todesstrafe zuerkennt’. Vgl. Gl Hochverrat 2; Wergeld 10—11a

If the addition, which is equivalent to on folces folcriht (Mirce 3), conceals a special sense going beyond ‘according to common law, customary in the land’, it means: ‘according to old theoretical tradition, which applies only if the matter comes to court at all, which as a rule is not the case, since the slain king is either avenged in blood by his kin or his retinue, or statutory royal law sentences the murderer to death’. Cf. Gl Hochverrat 2; Wergeld 10—11a

innc mid Englum braucht Grið 4 geradezu im Ggs. zur Denalagu; es liegt hier also ein deutlicher Missgriff durch hlq vor—vermutlich infolge der Unverständlichkeit des Volksnamens—, den man nicht etwa mit Schmid beseitigen darf, indem man ‘Angeln [im Ggs. zu Anglo-Sachsen und -Jüten]’ übs.: eine Bed., die im 10. Jh. erstorben war

Grið 4 uses innc mid Englum expressly in contrast to the Danelaw; here, then, there is a clear blunder by hlq — presumably because the name of the people was unintelligible — which one must not, say, remove with Schmid by translating ‘Angles [in contrast to Anglo-Saxons and Anglo-Jutes]’: a meaning that had died out by the 10th cent.

Die Hälfte fürs Volk vergleicht Schreuer (Verbrechenskonk. 94) mit der Injurienbusse für Missachtung, die andere für die Sippe mit der Deliktsbusse: m. E. nicht zutreffend.—Letztere 15000 werden auch für den erschlagenen Prinzen fällig; u. 2⁴. Diese Hälfte heisst ‘einfach’ Mirce 2

Schreuer (Verbrechenskonk. 94) compares the half for the people with the compensation for insult for contempt, and the other, for the kindred, with the compensation for the offence: in my opinion not correct. — The latter 15000 also fall due for a slain prince; below 2⁴. This half is called ‘single’ in Mirce 2

Is wergildes in D or weres in hlq archetypal? In the following line wer stands in both classes of MSS for wergild in this narrower sense. — The meaning that Toller Suppl. 140 posits for cynedom IIIa, ‘a fine paid for the offence to the royal dignity’, need not be assumed: ‘dignity’ suffices
